Although the connections between COVID-19 and cardiovascular inflammation in pregnant women require more exploration, this modest review focuses on the probable pathways by which SARSCoV-2 infects its host, particularly in pregnant women with cardiovascular illness.

articleTitle: The Particularities of Using Enzymatic Debridement Therapy in Deep Burns Treatment According to Functional Regions
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Enzymatic debridement is an effective minimal invasive method in deep burns treatment, proving good results in eschar removal. In our retrospective study, we included 12 patients, hospitalized in the Burn Department from the “ Sf. Spiridon” Emergency Country Hospital Iasi, during a 2-year period (2019-2020), which match on the application criteria for enzymatic debridement treatment. As an alternative to surgical treatment, enzymatic debridement has been proved as an important tool, reducing the number of hospitalisation days, as well as the bleeding, and thus saving the donor sites.

articleTitle: Study on Choice Reaction Time as a Complementary Method in Idiopathic Orofacial Pain
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Taking into consideration that investigations of cognitive performance in chronic pain is under researched, especially the area for neuropathic pain patients which is very poor, the paper herein has the main objective to analyze an Idiopathic Orofacial Pain (IOFP) correlation with a quantifiable increase in latency when performing complex CRT tests compared to the standard values of a healthy individual of the same gender and chronological age. Hence, it is presented a study built on a specific literature and based on the hypothesis that five elements associated IOFP pathologies, as menopause, age>50 years, depression and/or anxiety, mild cognitive impairment (nonamnestic), chronic pain syndrome, may modify CRT tests in order to provide the CRT argument as a complementary way to IOFP stratification. This study opens up new scientific perspectives to be validated in terms of IOFP behavioral and cognitive assessments, as well as to new advanced CRT system implementations in the eHealth regime.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks for Medical Image Super-resolution
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Super-resolution (SR) techniques are very useful in enhancing low resolution images. This becomes even more effective when the clinicians and radiologists need to detect tiny bone fractures in some low-resolution medical images such as X-Rays. In this short paper, the application of new deep learning single-image SR techniques to medical bone X-Ray images have been investigated. The quality of the results, when applied to plain hand X-Rays, are assessed based on peak signal-to-noise ratio and mean opinion score (MOS) and the superiority of generative adversarial networks (GANs), particularly in terms of MOS, has been verified for such applications.

articleTitle: Synthetic Mesh Used in Open Incisional Hernia Repair Following Initial Abdominal Surgery
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Anatomically, the abdominal anterolateral wall has several week points prone to herniation. Moreover, after surgical interventions, an increased intra-abdominal pressure may lead to extravasation of the abdominal content through the operated site, protruding under the skin and leading to an incisional hernia. We have analyzed retrospectively 203 abdominal incisional hernia repairs that the first author operated at “Dr. Iacob Czihac” Military Emergency Clinical Hospital, Iasi, Romania, between 2008 and 2018. Open surgical repair was done with sublay non-absorbable polypropylene mash, and the placement depended on the hernia particularities: perioblilical retromuscular (53 cases), median subombilical properitoneal (84 cases), median intraperitoneal (2 cases with gigantic hernias), and lateral retromuscular (64 cases). Associated health problems of patients were addressed properly by surgical and anesthetic teams. No complications that needed surgical re-intervention after mesh placement were encountered. At less than 1 year, 5 patients, and between 1 and 3 years, other 3 more patients, required reintervention.

articleTitle: Swelling Analysis of Thermal and Chemical Crosslinked Konjac Glucomannan/Gellan Gum Cardiac Patch
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the first cause of death worldwide. Within these, myocardial infarction is particularly limiting to patients. Although different therapies are used for myocardial infarction, the restoration of myocardial tissue and normal heart function is the desirable objective for tissue engineering. Currently, bioprinting is gaining more interest in this area for its many advantages. For this reason, we determined and compared the swelling degree and porosity of non-bioprinted and bioprinted patches. The produced patches had a high degree of swelling and exhibited very porous structures, indicating that the proposed formulation is very interesting for myocardial tissue engineering. Results also indicated that the bioprinting process allowed us to have more control over the final internal structure of the patch.

articleTitle: Custom-Made Cutting Blocks for Total Knee Arthroplasty: Two Case Reports and Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The custom-made cutting guide technique is useful in arthroplasties for patiens with complex deformed knees. We describe two cases of severe knee osteoarthritis, successfully managed with VISIONAIRE cutting guides for the total knee arthroplasty.

articleTitle: Fake News Management in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Fake news has gained significant ground in the political sector, since 2016 American elections, followed by Brexit disinformation. The COVID ‘19 pandemic was the catalyst in healthcare, by spreading false information regarding the Corona virus. Thus, the issue of fake news became not as trivial as the impact of such information into other fields, as we are talking about people’s lives at stake. Therefore, it is of uttermost importance to combat fake news in healthcare, but also in the medical act – as not only the patient is subject to disinformation, but medical personnel as well. Moreover, it is preferable to repel any type of false information regarding the healthcare act, before it gets widespread, to the public, to suppress its possible effects, which can be life threatening. The paper starts with a presentation of the existing work in the field of fake news in healthcare. We then present a set of data used for testing the proposed model. Then, we describe a model of a system for detection of fake news in the healthcare domain. The study ends with a comparison of the obtained results with other existing implementations, followed by future directions of research and the conclusions of our study.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Variants in Romanian Population – a Genome-Wide Association Study
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Worldwide, lung cancer is the deadliest malignant tumour, being associated with a major risk factor: smoking. The exposure to environmental risk factors does not explain completely the development of lung malignant tumours, raising questions about the influence of the genetic background and the interaction between genes and environment. The study aims to identify variants which are associated with lung cancer in the Romanian population. After an association analysis performed in R Studio using PLINK tool for the genomic data obtained from 1386 cases and 1437 control subjects, 69 single nucleotide polymorphisms having a p value below 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> were identified, 4 of which had a p value below 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup>. None of the variants identified has been previously reported as connected to lung cancer. After an investigation of the scientific literature regarding the genes where the statistically significant single nucleotide polymorphisms are located, multiple connections to lung cancer were identified.

articleTitle: Medical Rehabilitation System Based on Depth Camera: vINCI study
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: As we get older, various health-related problems appear, and it becomes more and more difficult to perform actions that once seemed simple. This paper presents a novel solution for different mobility and age-related problems, that incorporates virtual reality and video gaming features. The main feature provided by the implemented rehabilitation system is given by the multitude of exercises and the infinite possible combinations to cover a wide range of locomotor disorders and the virtual avatar capable of reproducing complex and flawless movements recorded using depth cameras. The novelty is also given by the chosen technologies, the almost real virtual environment and the architecture based on microservices.

articleTitle: A Finite Element Head Model Based on Chinese Visible Human Dataset for Electromagnetic Simulations of Magnetic Induction Measurement
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Magnetic induction measurement (MIM) is a promising technique for craniocerebral diseases detection with attractive advantages compared with CT and MRI. We propose a convenient method for constructing finite element head model that is applied to perform electromagnetic simulations of MIM. A finite element head model with high mesh quality based on the second Chinese Visible Human dataset is reported for the first time. The head model involves seven tissues, including muscle, bone, brain grey matter, brain white mater, cerebrospinal fluid, cerebellum, and eyeball. It has a good generality and can be imported into various electromagnetic analysis software based on finite element method while only a small amount of computing resources will be consumed.

articleTitle: A Broadband Approach for the Generation and Reception of Low-Frequency Ultrasounds In-Air for Sonar Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: In-air ultrasonic transducers are mostly characterized by a narrow frequency band, which limits the performances of sonar systems. Broadband transducers are widely investigated, but it still represents a technological bottle neck. Recently, we proposed a biologically inspired ultrasonic transducer, with interesting characteristics in terms of bandwidth and directionality. Considering the above, standard electronics can be revisited using alternative approaches. The work presents the development a broadband system for the generation/reception of ultrasounds in-air. It is based on spiral shaped, polyvinylidene-fluoride (PVDF) broadband transducers for the generation and reception ultrasounds in air, and second-generation voltage conveyor (VCII) based electronic interfaces in transmission and reception. The latter exploits their inherent broadband characteristics and the capability of working in voltage and current mode, to operate with a bandwidth larger than 60 kHz.

articleTitle: On the Interactions Between Bovine Serum Albumin and Reduced Glutathione in Solution
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The intrinsic viscosity and interactions between bovine serum albumin (BSA) and reduced glutathione (GSH) in buffer solutions at 37°C and pH = 7.4 were determined and discussed. The presence of GSH in the BSA solutions changes the interactions between the unlike molecules in solution, but zeta potential remains unchanged. Due to the specific interactions induced by GSH, the dependences of the specific viscosity as a function of a dimensionless parameter, concentration $\times$ intrinsic viscosity, cannot be included in a master curve. The slope increase is an indicative of hierarchical self-assembly. Thus, this study reveals new facets of glutathione in living cells.

articleTitle: Rule-based Health Status Evaluation System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: In this paper we present a rule-based generic model for health status evaluation. Considering that the physiological measurements are related to the physical activity that the monitored patient performs, the normal threshold ranges can be used for health status evaluation only when the patient is sitting quietly. For the activities with different intensities, different threshold ranges must be considered as normal ranges. Using the MET (Metabolic Equivalent of Tasks) score of each physical activity, proposed system automatically extracts the threshold ranges in the form of rules for each monitored vital sign for each physical activity known by the system. The system performance was evaluated using PAMAP2 dataset and showing the promising results.

articleTitle: Edmonds’ Blossom Algorithm Analysis in a Medical Emergency Management System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: This paper research is focused on the use of a matching algorithm, from graph theory, over an emergency medical system. The application architecture is divided across multiple modules, communicating between them in real time: ambulance level module, hospital level modules, central module (medical center, in charge of deciding the hospital/s compatible to the accident), traffic center module (in charge of deciding the route towards the chosen hospital). The experimental results, for both implementation approaches, sequential and parallel, have proven that for Blossom algorithm, a more scalable solution regarding the number of simultaneous accidents, is represented by the parallel implementation.

articleTitle: A Fractal Approach to Streamline the Management of Hospital Information Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The paper proposes solutions to improve HIS management speculating the advantages of a fractal multi-agent system holonic architecture. A case study aimed at adapting a hospital for hybrid operations (COVID / non-COVID) demonstrated the effectiveness of capitalizing on the properties of self-similarity and self-organization in solving specific problems of tracking information and patients flows.

articleTitle: Comparison of Automated Pipelines for Nanopore 16S Sequencing Data Analysis of Human Gut Microbiota Samples
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) enables characterization of complex microbial communities through metagenomic techniques. Metagenomics generally employs sequencing of multiple samples at once, through barcoding techniques, with subsequent reads of each sample being demultiplexed by specialized software. Third generation NGS equipment such as the Oxford Nanopore (ONT) technology has been developed to reduce costs, turnaround time and complex bioinformatics. For ONT, several bioinformatic workflows are available, with various tools for each step such as demultiplexing, classification of reads, polishing, mapping and visualization, which are successively applied on raw data. The performance and results of the workflows vary, especially considering the fact that ONT presents a 10-15% error rate, with short reads and around 5% with long reads. Here, we compare the results of two different workflows (Nanopore’s EPI2ME and NanoCLUST platforms) for real-world 16S human gut microbiota samples.

articleTitle: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) Application for Heavy Metals Removal from Wastewaters using Conventional and Microbial Sorbents
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Heavy metals represent a category of pollutants generated by both natural and anthropic sources with serious negative health and environmental impacts. Their removal from wastewaters remains a challenge still, especially at low concentrations. Adsorption of metal ions using conventional and non-conventional sorbents including microorganisms, is one of the frequently applied and studied removal technologies. However, the available scientific literature offers insufficient data regarding the sustainability of this process using various types of materials. Therefore, the current study aims to analyze and compare the available research concerning the environmental impacts of conventional and microbial-based adsorbents. In this sense, a closer perspective is given to the application of Life Cycle Assessment methodology (LCA).

articleTitle: The Development of a Brain-Computer Interface for Controlling a Robotic Arm and a Mobile Device by Using the Voluntary Eye Blinking
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Exploring the challenges raised by the brain-computer interface (BCI) multidisciplinary field, this paper provides a real-time LabVIEW application for controlling a six degrees robotic arm using the NI myRIO development board and the NeuroSky Mindwave Mobile portable headset. By detecting and numbering the consecutive, voluntary eye-blinks, the necessary commands accomplished two different approaches of controlling the robotic arm. The proposed solution encompasses a completely functional BCI experimental prototype based on a simple working principle, straightforward control mode, realtime running, friendly graphical user interface, and effective communication between hardware and software-enabled by LabVIEW graphical programming environment. An additional feature of the proposed brain-computer interface system is the mobile robot underlying the robotic arm so that people with neuromotor disabilities can benefit from a versatile assistive biomechatronic device.

articleTitle: Methacrylated Collagen/Chitosan - Based Hydrogels as Scaffolds for Soft Tissue Engineering
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Hidrogels are three-dimensional networks with excellent hydrophilic characteristics, which mimic the EMC of the soft tissues and make them interesting materials for tissues regeneration. In this paper, methacrylated collagen/chitosan - based hydrogels, crosslinked with poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate have been prepared and characterized in order to be used as scaffolds for soft tissue engineering. The three-dimensional structure, high hydrophilicity and macroporosity are characteristics that recommend these hydrogels for tissue regeneration. The synthetic polymer reacted with methacrylated collagen and methacrylated chitosan causing a significant increase pore diameter which is suitable for cell growth and proliferation. The biodegradation studies have shown that hydrogel scaffolds are susceptible to enzymatic attack under simulated physiological conditions of pH and temperature and the cytocompatibility tests indicate good cell-material interactions with fibroblasts.

articleTitle: A Support Process of Telemedicine Applications that Integrates a Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: With the help of telemedicine, patients can be treated by remote specialists through teleconference. In addition to the communication between health professionals and their patients, telemedicine should coordinate and manage the day-to-day operations and it must have a well-defined service request and incident management process. A support process that includes service request and incident management helps telemedicine to prevent problems, to identify rapidly the causes of problems when they occur and to help in remediating the issues. To allow faster support and help from the system to the patients in an automated and user-friendly approach, the service request and incident management process should integrate a chatbot.

articleTitle: Preprocessing of Electrocardiogram Techniques – A Review
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: This paper aims to highlight some techniques for improving the acquisition of ECG signals that can be subsequently analyzed and processed efficiently using software that contains visualization and filtering tools. The study of the ECG signal includes the generation and simulation of a signal, which is to be processed and the extraction of some characteristics by comparison between different algorithms as well as signal analysis techniques. It is also possible to create and detect certain artifacts that may appear during recordings. The software applications that provide such a toolkit for signal processing are developed under MATLAB programming environment. We also used LabVIEW - a graphical programming tool noted for programming by means of the structure of graphical blocks, which can provide a view of all elements built into the workspace, and an overview of the front panel.

articleTitle: Application of a Multilayer Perceptron Neural Network for Differentiation of the Influence of Ankle Stretch Duration for Hemiplegic Affected Ankle Dorsiflexion Quantified by a Smartphone Functioning as a Wearable and Wireless Gyroscope Platform
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The amalgamation of wearable and wireless inertial sensor systems and machine learning with accessibility to Cloud computing resources offers the opportunity to substantially advance the efficacy of a therapeutic rehabilitation intervention. The smartphone represents a wearable and wireless inertial sensor system equipped with a gyroscope for the acquisition of clinically perceptible signal data. Machine learning, such as a multilayer perceptron neural network, can provide definitive distinction of an assortment of therapeutic prescriptions. With Cloud computing accessibility a subject and clinical team supervising the therapy endeavor can perform their roles in a remote Internet connected context. For example, a subject with a hemiplegic affected ankle can undergo a series of prescribed ankle stretch durations using a wedge board. The subsequent ability to conduct dorsiflexion of the hemiplegic affected ankle can be quantified through a smartphone functioning as a wearable and wireless gyroscope platform. The gyroscope signal data can be consolidated to a feature set for machine learning classification, and a multilayer perceptron neural network can be applied. Considerable classification accuracy has been attained to distinguish between an assortment of ankle stretch durations through a wedge board for hemiplegic affected ankle dorsiflexion quantified by a smartphone serving as a wearable and wireless gyroscope platform. The implications of the amalgamation of wearable and wireless inertial sensor systems with machine learning and the synergy with Cloud computing resources infer a highly interactive therapeutic intervention experience with significantly augmented clinical situational awareness for improved determination of therapy efficacy.

articleTitle: Recovery of Valuable Heavy Metals from Polluted Soil Using Phytomining Process - A New Challenge for Earning Secondary Raw Materials and Health Risk Reduction
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Phytomining is an innovative application of phytoremediation process that involves accumulators or hyperaccumulator plants grown in polluted soils, being able to accumulate high concentration of metals in their tissues, where from valuable heavy metals (e.g. nickel, cobalt, copper, zinc) will be recovered by biomass processing. This technology can be successfully applied to treat contaminated soils with low to moderate metal concentrations and fast-growing plants are usually required to ensure high biomass and efficient metal uptake. Phytomining involves lower costs compared to conventional methods such as mining, and contributes both to the remediation of contaminated soils and provides additional beneficial resources that can be used as raw material in other processes from industry. After harvesting the plants, heavy metals are extracted either by biomass incineration, microbial fermentation, extraction or by chemical treatments. The main objective of this paper is to describe and highlight the importance of phytomining process in cleaning-up the polluted media by phytoextraction and recovery of valuable heavy metals from biomass of the selected plants.

articleTitle: Is Short-Term Heart Rate Variability Good Enough to Predict Vascular Events in Hypertensive Patients?
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Vascular events are the main cause of premature death and disability in the developed countries, where there is great interest in the development of computational tools for their early detection. A very relevant variable for their study is the heart rate, that can be analyzed through heart rate variability (HRV). Furthermore, high blood pressure is an important risk factor for most cardiovascular diseases. In fact, small reductions in blood pressure are known to markedly reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This study evaluates the predictive value of short-term HRV (STHRV) by developing models based on data mining algorithms to stratify the risk of vascular events from hypertensive patients. For this specific framework, the performance of various machine learning models (Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, Gaussian Naive Bayes, KN Nearest Neighbours and Logistic regression), trained with different time lengths of 5, 30 and 60 minutes of HRV features during sleep stage was compared. The analyzed HRV parameters were associated to time, frequency and nonlinear features. A total of 139 Holter recordings from hypertensive patients of whom 17 developed a vascular event were analyzed. Results indicated that classification models developed using STHRV, with only 5 minutes length, provided similar or even better results than those developed with longer time series. Furthermore, the STHRV models provided a higher sensitivity and a slightly higher F1 score. The best one, based on Support Vector Machines, yielded 88.2% sensitivity and 75% F1 score. Thus, this research suggests the feasibility of STHRV analysis for risk stratification of hypertensive patients to anticipate serious vascular events.

articleTitle: Aberrations Assessment of Progressive Lens Using an Educational Aberrometer
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: In the article, we review the different mechanisms of aberrations that can show up in the progressive lens and affect foveal vision, peripheral vision, and binocular vision. Because of the complex phenomena of the aberrations in the progressive lens, we decided to use an experimental method and, therefore, we introduce a new concept of an educational aberrometer for the progressive lens.

articleTitle: Least Squares Differential Quadrature Method for Systems of Fractional Order Differential Equations
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: In the present paper we apply the Least Squares Differential Quadrature Method (LSDQM) in order to find approximate analytical solutions for systems of fractional order differential equations (FODEs). We compare the obtained solution with the exact solution of the considered problems at integer orders and we compute the maximum absolute error to demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Application of Latent Semantic Analysis and Supervised Learning Methods to Automate Triage of Referral Letters for Spinal Surgery
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Referral letters are the most common mean used by healthcare practitioners to exchange information relevant to patient care. However, their triage takes a significant amount of administrative resources, which may be amenable to automation. This study aims to evaluate a pilot study for automating the triage of referral letters sent to a spine surgery department in secondary care using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and supervised machine learning methods. Text data in referral letters were represented using Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) scores and Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) and fed into supervised learning models to classify it into urgent and non-urgent. Their outcomes have been evaluated using performance metrics (precision, recall, F1, area under the curve (AUC), and accuracy), and their clinical value is assessed based on decision curve analysis. The AdaBoost classifier obtained the maximum AUC score (61.8%) in the test set. The model also reached an F1 score of 53.1% with 48.6% and 58.6% of recall and precision scores, respectively. Comparing its net benefit against baseline clinical alternatives proves that the model has potential clinical value, and it might be a valuable tool for automating the referrals’ triaging process. This study successfully demonstrated the potential for automating the triage of referrals and provides a foundation for further work.

articleTitle: Cephalic Pancreatoduodenectomy (CPD) Performed for Pancreatic Head Adenocarcinoma in a 72 Year- Old Patient - Case Presentation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: We are presenting a case of mechanical jaundice caused by a pancreatic head cancer in a 72-year-old patient. The clinical examination suspected this diagnosis based on the characteristics of jaundice and the Courvoisier-Terrier sign that was present in the clinical exam. Laboratory and imagistic exams confirm this suspicion. After a short preoperative preparation, a cephalic pancreatoduodenectomy was made using the Whipple procedure. The postoperative evolution was complicated by the appearance of a biliary fistula, which closed after the resuming of intestinal transit. The patient left the surgery department after 25 days of hospitalization. Technological advancement, adequate preoperative rebalancing and especially the emergence of surgical centers specialized in pancreatic resections, have reduced mortality after CPD below 5%. However, an unresolved issue is the long-term survival after CPD for pancreatic cancer (0 – 24%), which is considered by some authors disappointing.

articleTitle: Modular Rotating-hinge Prosthesis in Severe Haemophilic Valgus Knee Osteoarthritis. Case Presentation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: We report a successful case of a patient with type A haemophilia, with advanced valgus knee osteoarthritis. The patient underwent surgery with metaphyseal cemented modular rotating hinge prosthesis type RT-PLUS Modular® and Moroctocog Alpha substitution treatment for effective hemostasis.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Automatic Food Logging for Health Applications Based on Video Camera Glasses
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Dietary monitoring can provide valuable information for individuals, while aggregated information from diet logs is important for public health. Although several food logging systems have been presented in the scientific literature, a small number have employed smartglasses. In this paper, we introduce eyewear-based software architecture for tag extraction from video by using several machine learning models. We demonstrate our software architecture with a system designed to help smart eyewear users to perform food logging in an automatic, passive way. Also, we conduct an experiment to report the performance of our system in various conditions.

articleTitle: Serious Games used in Rehabilitation of Patients with Osteoarthritis
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The degenerative rheumatic disease to the hip joint is common in the elderly population. Diseases of the hip joint affect the functionality of the lower limb. This disability leads to a decrease in the quality of life, specifically to both the somatic and the psychic components, being marked by the traumatic effects represented by pain, stability deficit, and mobility deficit, having a major disabling character. By applying the medical rehabilitation program based on serious games can improve the general condition of the patient, increase mobility in the hip joint, increase the strength of the hip muscles, and reeducation of gait. The main objective of this paper is to present the use of the exergames-based program as a method of physical therapy in the treatment of degenerative rheumatic disease of the hip joint. Also, this paper presents a study on 12 patients with degenerative rheumatic disease in the hip joint and the efficiency of the physical therapy using serious games.

articleTitle: Wearable Biopotential Acquisition Module For mHealth Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Nowadays, wearable devices are becoming more and more present in medical applications. Wearable sensors integrated in complex mobile health (mHealth) systems are starting to change the traditional healthcare approach into a smart healthcare system centered on the patient. Hence, remote and continuous acquisition of physiological signals by such mHealth systems can increase prevention and early detection of health problems, reducing the cost of care. In this paper, a mobile biopotential acquisition system with three textile electrodes embedded in a T-shirt is developed. For performance evaluation purposes, the physiological electrical signal generated by the heart, the electrocardiogram (ECG) signal, is recorded both with the proposed mobile acquisition system with textile electrodes and with the standard acquisition systems that uses common AgCl disposable electrodes. The experimental results prove that the proposed mobile acquisition system can achieve similar performance with the standard approach, in recording robust physiological signals.

articleTitle: A New Step in Detecting and Preventing Hereditary Cancer: the Hope Project and Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The article is a study based on the Hope project, (Erasmus+ programme), which is being implemented by an international partnership of medical universities, healthcare centres, non-governmental educational organisations and IT centres from Bulgaria, France, Hungary and Romania. The HOPE project (2018-1-RO01-KA202-049189) focuses on oncogenetics and raises awareness about the importance of using family history as a screening tool in detecting and preventing cancer. The article presents the HOPE mobile application, which calculates a person’s risk of developing hereditary cancer, and gives insights into the feedback given by the participants who tested the usability of the application.

articleTitle: Microstates as a Tool for Identifying Dreaming in a Sleep EEG
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Sleep plays an important role in both physical and mental health. One of its parts is also dreaming. It is possible that dreaming helps us with memory consolidation, coping with experiences, and more. But the exact meaning of dreaming has not yet been described. If we are able to identify the time when dreaming occurs, then the electrical activity of the brain could explain the processes that are connected with dreaming and their effect on the body. In this study, we propose an approach to identify dreaming using short event analysis of microstates and its classification by the k-NN method.

articleTitle: In Vitro Evaluation of Paclitaxel Loaded Magnetic Nanoparticles for Breast Cancer Therapy
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: This paper presents in vitro evaluation of several characteristics of Paclitaxel loaded magnetic nanoparticles based on iron oxide nanosferes and biotinylated N-palmitoyl chitosan for potential applications as drug delivery system in breast cancer therapy. Obtained magnetic nanoparticles were dispersible in glucose solution (10 %), induced apoptosis in MDA-MB-231 cells and they did not determine notable modification of the coagulation parameter (time of partially activated thromboplastin-APTT) after the contact with blood. In the presence of a magnetic field, the nanoparticles aligned in the direction of the field lines. (Abstract)

articleTitle: EEG Preprocessing Methods for BCI Imagined Speech Signals
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Brain Computer Interface (BCI) is a computer-based system that acquires signals from the brain, preprocesses the collected signals and then translate the input into commands sent to the effectors. Acquiring signals from the surface of the brain is a difficult task due to the low amplitude electric processes that occur. The recorded waves are usually contaminated with other biosignals with higher amplitude. These artefacts affect the quality of the signals leading to difficulty in decoding the desired brain activities. In this paper we focus on eliminating the electrooculogram from the electroencephalogram signals collected during imagined speech. We compared two preprocessing methods: the Adaptive Filter and Principal Component Analysis decomposition and concluded that both methods improve the quality of the EEG signals. However, the developed PCA method turned out to offer better results regarding the correlation between signals from the same class.

articleTitle: Development and Functioning of a Regional Diabetic Retinopathy Register in the City of Varna, Bulgaria – First Results
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: This study presents the first results related to the development and functioning of a regional diabetic retinopathy (DR) population-based registry in the city of Varna, Bulgaria. A specialized software has been developed for entering, storing, and management of information of DR patients. The registry started functioning on January 4, 2021 and only permanently living in the city of Varna people over the age of 17 diagnosed with diabetes were entered into the registry. Screening for DR was conducted through one of the following diagnostic methods: indirect ophthalmoscopy, retinal fundus photography with a stationary or portable fundus camera. Detailed information on the screening method and process, the type of the DR, treatment, along with data for the diabetes of the patients are stored in the records. In total 230 patients are screened for DR for a period of 10 months. The mean age of the patients who were screened (n=230) is 63.2±17.8 years, lower for men 61 (12.6) than for women 65 (30.1) years, t=4.473, p=0.035. The total number of patients with DR was 90. Among the 230 screened persons with diabetes 30 were newly diagnosed with DR. The establishment of a regional registry of patients with DR provides an opportunity for early detection of DR, information on the prevalence of DR and the effectiveness of treatment, and can serve as a basis for the development of a national screening program and registry.

articleTitle: Follow-up of Women Treated with LLETZ using Two Sensitive Molecular Assays
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: There is scientific evidence that HPV testing after therapy can predict treatment failure with significantly higher sensitivity and similar specificity compared to repeated cytology and histological status of the margins. Given the risk of recurrence of HPV infection, it is necessary to develop patient follow-up protocols, depending on the DNA / HPV status and that of cytology. We presented here 3 cases which were followed-up closely with sensitive assays after surgical intervention. The superiority of excision surgery in the case of intraepithelial cervical neoplasia is given by the success rate of the therapy. One of the most important and actual one is large loop excision of transformation zone. To predict treatment failure with significantly higher sensitivity and similar specificity compared to repeated cytology and histological status of the margins, we should repeat the testing with less invasion, especially HPV testing after therapy. The goal of these research is to establish new algorithms for successful testing and follow-up of treated women.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of Hip Disarticulation Prosthesis Based on Computerized Metrics. Case Study
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Lower limb prostheses must replace the structure, function, and aesthetics of the missing limb. For hip disarticulation, the path to functional prosthesis use can be long and challenging because of the inherent difficulty of ambulation when the entire lower limb has been lost. The energy requirements of prosthesis use in such situations are as much as twice that of normal ambulation [1]. The paper aims to present the difficulties met in the process of lower limb prosthetic fitting, focusing on constructive-functional aspects of hip disarticulation prostheses and the information provided by the analysis of biomechanical parameters and physiological parameters.

articleTitle: Analysis of Antimicrobial Resistance and Sensitivity Patterns for E.Coli and S. Aureus using a Mutual Information Score
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has become a global problem in both human and veterinary medicine which means new efforts are mandatory to understand and control AMR. Thus, the development of new computer tools for a better understanding of this biological phenomenon is needed. This paper aims to analyze patterns of cross-resistance and collateral sensitivity using mutual information scores and networks of interaction between antibiotics belonging to the same class or different classes. The analysis is conducted for data corresponding to different strains of Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus).

articleTitle: Machine Learning Classification of Hemiplegic Dorsiflexion Based on Knee Orientation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The development of wearable systems equipped with inertial sensors offers the opportunity to promote a highly patient-specific rehabilitation experience, for which customized therapy response can be quantified. For example, the smartphone with its gyroscope sensor can provide extremely informative signal data respective of the progressive rehabilitation experience. Since the ability to dorsiflex the ankle is impaired by hemiparesis, this dysfunction impacts the characteristics of gait. The repetitive prescription of dorsiflexion enables a therapeutic pathway for the advancement of the hemiplegic affected ankle. However, there are multiple influences the ability to dorsiflex the ankle, such as the correlated knee joint orientation. Using the smartphone as a wearable and wireless gyroscope platform the ability to dorsiflex the hemiplegic affected ankle in conjunction with a series of knee joint orientations are quantified and post-processed to a feature set for machine learning classification incorporating a multilayer perceptron neural network. Considerable classification accuracy has been achieved for the distinction of an assortment of knee joint positions influencing the ability to dorsiflex the hemiplegic affected ankle. The implications infer highly interactive and sophisticated therapeutic intervention with augmented situational awareness for the clinical therapy team in consideration of a patient’s unique rehabilitation requirements.

articleTitle: Quality Management in Design Telemedicine Service for Children in Home Mechanical Ventilation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: This paper presents a clinical implementation of a telemonitoring service for home ventilated patients. In particular, a methodology was defined for approaching the problem considering clinical and technological requirements as well as legal aspects mainly related to security and privacy of patient data. The use of design methodologies based on quality management (PDCA and process modelling) has been proved to be a valid approach for the clinical success of the telemedicine service.

articleTitle: Mobile App to Make Better the Obesity Prevention Process in Adolescents
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Currently the whole world is going through an epidemiological crisis due to Covid-19, a virus which has a greater impact on people who are overweight or obese. Obesity represents a risk factor for serious illness and death from COVID-19. There is an enzyme that converts angiotesin-2, which is an enzyme that SARS-CoV-2 uses for entry at the cellular level, it is found in higher amounts in people with obesity. Among the group of people who can suffer from obesity are adolescents, who do not always maintain healthy eating habits or perform physical activities. In this research, a mobile application is presented to control and monitor the patient's body mass index according to their weight and height, making it known if they have obesity or any variant. In addition, it allows the patient to know the appropriate portions of daily food and to keep an own control of their physical activities and a history of their meals. That is why the objective of this research is to determine the impact that a mobile application can have on the obesity prevention process in adolescents. This study was carried out in Lima in 56 adolescents from 10 to 19 years old, in which 44.6% managed to improve their condition and 26.7% managed to stay in a normal condition.

articleTitle: Facial Expressions Recognition by Structuring the Embeddings Space
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Lately, Facial Expression Recognition (FER) gained in popularity in the medical field due to their importance in understanding the human psychology or detecting various pathologies. In this paper, we propose a more efficient solution for recognizing facial expressions using a more convenient structuring of the data. To accomplish this aspect, a clustering loss entitled Large Margin was used in addition to the classic Cross Entropy, in order to improve discrimination in the embeddings space. The main study consisted of trying different distance metrics (L1, L2, cosine similarity) between embeddings, to examine which of them offers a better structuring of the data. The solution is tested on two benchmarks with very good results.

articleTitle: Mechanical Testing Following the Application of Polymers on Different Types of Screws Used to Fix Osteoporotic Bone
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The mechanical tests aimed to evaluate the behavior of different screws, used as osteosynthesis material, after covering them with a polymeric film and used for fixing in block of synthetic bone that simulates the structure of osteoporotic bone. The traction forces applied to cause the fracture and the displacements caused by them were recorded by a specialized program WDW Universal Testing Machine and Control System. In conclusion by applying a polyurethane acrylic polymer coating, an efficient transition medium between the screw and the bone is ensured, which leads to improved cohesion between them, ultimately increasing the stability of the fracture. The addition of hydroxyapatite, a component of bone, to the polymer mass has advantages especially for the 10% concentration.

articleTitle: Method Development for Visible Spectrophotometric Analysis of Ibuprofen in Pharmaceuticals
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Ibuprofen is a prominent member of the group of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), with good anti-inflammatory action, a very effective analgesic, with increased antipyretic effect. The aim of this research was to exactly quantify pure Ibuprofen content in tablets of a pharmaceutical, by a spectrophotometric analysis method in the Visible range. Ibuprofen was quantitatively converted to a bright orange dye with a yellowish shade, by a color reaction with alphanaphthylamine in the presence of sodium nitrite, in an absolute ethanol medium. Following the analysis, it was found 397.952 milligrams of pure Ibuprofen content /film-coated tablet of the pharmaceutical product. This value was very close to Ibuprofen content declared by the pharmaceutical manufacturer (400 milligrams), with a mean deviation of only 0.512 percent from the officially declared amount of active substance. The value found fits perfectly within the normal limits provided by the European and International Pharmacopoeias standards, taken over by the Romanian Pharmacopoeia, 10th Edition. The spectrophotometric analysis method was then successfully subjected to statistical analysis.

articleTitle: Video 360-Degree in Medical Teaching: from Script to Education Deployment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic catalyzed a dramatic change in medical education paradigm, mediating a wider use of technology and adoption of open education models. In this paper, we analyze the challenges encountered along the way from the production of educational 360-degree video scenarios to their actual use in medical teaching. Evaluation was two-fold: (a) medical students’ perception and attitude towards this technology and its actual effectiveness in teaching; (b) feed-back from the teachers and medical staff. The feed-back and concrete debriefing refer to the required one-semester course on emergency medicine taught during the autumn of 2020, when such videos were employed as a substitute for practical classes.

articleTitle: Identification of the Risks Generated in the Environment by Food Waste
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Today, it is estimated that about 88 million tonnes of food waste or 173 kilograms per capita are generated annually in the European Union. In farms, as well as in the processing and production industry, in shops, restaurants and households, food is lost and wasted along the entire food chain. Households are in the first place in the generation of food waste. Lost or wasted food contribute to climate change, with a global carbon footprint of about 8% of total global anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. Food waste is in fact a loss of resources, such as land, energy, water and others throughout the life cycle of products. For every kilogram of food produced, 4.5 kg of CO<inf>2</inf> are released into the atmosphere. Food waste has not only high social, economic and environmental costs, but also entails ethical consequences. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, 793 million people in the world are malnourished. Taking into account all these aspects, the central objective of this manuscript is to identify the risks generated in the environment by food waste in order to perform an analysis of food waste management options, which will then be evaluated in terms of: economic, ecological, social and technological by applying calculation tools.

articleTitle: Health Risk Assessment of Mercury in Cosmetics
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The main objective of this paper was to determine the mercury content within cosmetics and to assess the risk of intoxication with this heavy metal due to their use. We want to draw consumers' attention to the amount of mercury they are being daily exposed by using various cosmetics. A number of 7 sunscreens SPF 50+ for body and face samples from different manufacturers were selected from stores and pharmacies. The Advanced Mercury Analyzer 254 mercury analyzer with a detection limit of 0.00001 mg mercury was used to determine the mercury concentration. Our results indicate that sunscreens could be responsible for 30% from the alert level of the mercury. Even if this value does not seem high enough, we estimated that over the course of a year cosmetic products may account for up to 45% of the required level for side effects become manifest. This is especially worrisome if we consider that the human body is already being exposed to a significant amount of mercury in the food consumed daily. Based on this conclusion, in the future, it must be established whether the accumulation of mercury resulting from the multiple use of cosmetics can reach high potentially toxic levels.

articleTitle: Assesing Power Losses in Magnetic-Dielectric Tissues Exposed to Microwaves: Commercial Computational Software Capabilities and Limits
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Magnetite nanoparticles were detected in the human brain about 30 years ago. The contribution of their presence to the total absorbed power, when the human head is exposed to microwaves emitted by handheld communication devices, have not been quantified so far. It is the aim of the present work to assess, by simulation, the impact of the presence of magnetic material in dielectric tissues, by computing the electric and magnetic power losses and to highlight the peculiarities of the electromagnetic energy absorption calculation in such a situation.

articleTitle: Two-Channel Bioradar System for Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The development of accurate and reliable personal unobtrusive methods for detecting sleep breathing disorders, which have a huge impact on health and well-being of people, is an up-to-date task of modern sleep medicine. The recent studies proved the possibility of sleep disorders detection by means of bioradars. However, the problem of view dependency of the radar-based sleep monitor performance has not been solved jet. In the present paper, we proposed a two-bioradar system for sleep-disordered breathing detection. The system was validated in a sleep laboratory of Almazov National Medical Research Centre with the participation of 31 volunteers. We achieved accuracy and Cohen’s kappa of 75 and 66% for OSAS severity estimation, respectively. The results might contribute to creating methods for remote unobtrusive detection of sleep breathing disorders.

articleTitle: The Opportunity of Using Platelet Concentrates as an Adjuvant Tool for In-hospital Management of Bone Defects
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Bone defects are a frequent, difficult pathology and its clinical management can be quite challenging. The current therapeutic approach “of choice” is the autologous bone transfer, but this procedure is routinely burdened with complications and disadvantages, so an alternative solution, such as using platelet concentrates, has been extensively studied in recent decades. The current article consists of a systematic review of the scientific literature and an epidemiological analysis of data collected from the patients with bone defects who followed a treatment in the County Emergency Clinical Hospital “St. Spiridon”.The results of the review show that platelet concentrates are effective in 91.2% of the subjects included in this study, and the preparation technique is simple and cheap in the case of PRP and especially PRF. Although human subjects accounted for only 1.8%, in all cases, PRF was used and in all cases it proved its effectiveness. The results of the epidemiological study shows 42 patients with bone defects with a mean length of hospital stay of 17 days.In conclusion, platelet concentrates are effective in strengthening bone defects in the in vivo studies, but more studies are needed in human subjects. PRF is easier to prepare, more affordable than PRP and often shows a higher efficiency in bone healing. Since bone defects are a frequently encountered, complicated pathology that requires very high costs and long-term hospitalization, we consider that platelets deserve to be used in the hospital as an adjunct tool in the “fight” with bone defects.

articleTitle: Thermodynamic Studies of Pb(II) Ions Adsorption From Aqueous Solutions on Clay Adsorbent
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The removal of Pb(II) ions is an important issue for the treatment of industrial wastewater, due to its serious consequences on environment and human health. In this study a local clay material was used for the efficient removal of Pb(II) ions from aqueous solutions. The influence of initial Pb(II) ions concentration and temperature, was evaluated by batch adsorption technique. Langmuir and Dubinin-Radushkevich models were used to fit the equilibrium adsorption data and the statistical parameters depict a better and satisfactory correlation for Dubinin-Radushkevich model. Thermodynamic parameters revealed that the negative values of $\Delta \mathrm{G}^{\circ}$ and positive value of $\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}$ the adsorption process was spontaneous and endothermic. The experimental results indicate that clay adsorbent is promising alternative for removal of Pb(II) ions from industrial effluents.

articleTitle: Automated Assessment Implementation of Subcutaneous Adipose & Visceral Adipose Tissues in Human Abdominal Area
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: An implementation of a novel method to automate the assessment of the abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue and visceral adipose tissue which have been detected in MRI images for obese subjects is described. Deep learning has been exploited with a view of SAT / VAT quantification. The study aims to optimize the clinicians’ time. VAT results are promising.

articleTitle: Patient Simulators in Medical Education: New Enhancements II
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: A patient simulator (or a manikin) is designed to simulate the functional and physiological processes that take place in a living patient. It is primarily used by physicians, nurses, and other medical personnel to learn and train the technical and non-technical skills including improving communication skills. Simulators offer various features such as basic CPR training, the possibility of defibrillation, or blood pressure measurement by auscultation. This article describes the current shortcomings of patient simulators, in particular the lack of movement after defibrillation and the physical connection of the pressure cuff placed on the arm with the control computer located in the torso of the manikin. Furthermore, a deficiency in resuscitation torso QCPR (Quality Measurement Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) is described, where respiratory volumes are not measured. The aim of this work was to develop a system for the movement of the manikin after a defibrillation discharge, to implement the connection of the pressure cuff without the need for a physical connection to the torso of the manikin, and to extend the resuscitation torso so it measures the delivered gas volumes.

Author Keywords: gas flow meter in resuscitation torso

articleTitle: Cotinine and IL-6 - Biomarkers for Estimating Pharmacological Processes in Various Forms of Periodontitis
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Prunus spinosa L. is a medicinal plant found in the flora of many countries, especially in Central and Eastern Europe, being used for various pharmacological actions. In this study, the antioxidant properties of the species were evaluated on specific salivary biomarkers, in healthy volunteers, smokers and non-smokers, but also in subjects with periodontal disease using an aqueous extract obtained from the dried fruits of the harvested species from Tulcea County, Romania. The results obtained show that, regarding the two evaluated markers, cotinine and salivary interleukin 6 in groups of patients with superficial and deep chronic periodontal disease can serve as tools for evaluating the potential therapeutic effect of Prunus spinosa L. extract in the periodontal disease.

articleTitle: Object Manipulation for Assistive Robots
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: In robotic assistive environments, several capabilities are required, such as autonomous navigation, scene understanding and object manipulation that must be performed in safe condition. The paper presents a method for object manipulation based on the automatic identification of grasping points for a set of common objects, using colour and depth images acquired by the robot camera. Evaluation was performed in a simulation environment using the model of the TIAGo robot.

articleTitle: A Brief Review of Using the Inertial Sensor to Determine the Driver Head Posture
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The current paper presents an overview of the technical literature for the last 3 years of state-of-the-art driver behavior monitor systems based on inertial sensors. This paper presented the most suitable and performance applications that can be considered a relevant choice to determine with success the driver head activity based on the inertial sensor. The investigation of the technical domain was focused to determine the used acquisition method, computational method, and technique that was used to validate those systems/methods. The principal contribution provided by this paper is related to the fact that it provided a good overview of the last 3 years of used approaches, to monitor driver behavior with the help of the inertial sensor.

articleTitle: Combined Advantages of the Mobile Bearing Design and Cementless Fixation Technique for Total Knee Arthroplasty
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The mobile bearing (MB) design and the cementless technique offers specific advantages in total knee arthroplasty (TKA). We investigated the separate advantages of the mobile bearing design and cementless fixation and afterward reviewed studies that compare cementless MB TKA to cemented MB TKA in order to observ survivorship, clinical score, revision causes. We discovered that cementles MB TKA offers a longer survivorship, better clinical results, less revisions, all because of the combining techniques.

Author Keywords: mobile bearing cementless total knee arthroplasty

articleTitle: Data-Augmentation for Deep Learning Based Remote Photoplethysmography Methods
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Acquisition of remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) signals using deep learning-based methods has become very important for the measurement of heart rate (HR). These methods are known to require a large amount of data during training, so data augmentation is often used. In this paper we propose a methodology for data augmentation to be used as a pre-training step. We tested our proposed method using transfer-learning in three public databases, and we demonstrate that it helps the neural network to learn the main features of the videos. We improved the Mean Absolute Error by a factor of 3 using the small dataset UBFC-rPPG, by a factor of 2.5 in the medium-size dataset COHFACE and by a factor of 1.3 in the large dataset VIPL-HR.

articleTitle: Computational Power of Astrocytes and their Role in Neurobiology
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: It was considered previously that the behaviour of mammals was exclusively determined by the activity of neurons, while other brain cells such as astrocytes only offer support for neurons. Based on recent discoveries, the astrocytes have an important role in neurobiology. In particular, the astrocytes producing calcium are able to modulate neurotransmissions. Inspired by these connections between astrocytes and neurons, we define a formal model and show that under certain constrains this model has the same computational power as a Turing machine, being computationally complete.

articleTitle: Compact Rolling Walker Mechatronic System for Gait Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: In a society that is continuously ageing is a priority to design and develop technologies that assist the elder ones in the daily life. This paper presents the design consideration of a novel mechatronic device for efficient gait rehabilitation using commercial off-the-shelf components to ensure a competitive and affordable solution for the rising number of patients that need this type of therapy. The advantages of the current design and the design assumption are stated in the paper with experimental validation to be performed in the future. Three degrees of freedom actuators perform the moves necessary to re-educate the gait, packed in a rolling walker design. The device is built on the concept of an adaptable design that can morph around the patient to serve it’s needs and lead to a highly efficient treatment. The problem of different patient recovery pace and degree of disability was addressed by designing a device highly customizable at both mechanical and electronical level.

articleTitle: Thermal Characterizacion of Konjac/Gellam Gum Hydrogels for Cardiac Patch
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases and specifically myocardial infarction are one the public health challenges in our society. Although cardiac patches are currently a promising treatment approach, they have still room for improvement. In this sense, a better characterization of biomaterials used can improve its extra cellular matrix interaction and enhance both cell- and bioactive molecules-based therapies. For this reason, we proposed to use the TGA method to monitor the thermal stability and to understand the behavior of a konjac/gellam gum patch. This monitoring is represented by the thermal history, and in the case of hydrogels they determine it allows identifying the stages in which the hydrogel varies its behavior, either because some of the components escape from the hydrogel or because the structure is degraded.

articleTitle: Dynamic Changes of Perfusion Index During Hypoxemia and Hypercapnia in Outdoor Experiments
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Perfusion index (PI) derived from pulse oximetry is a well-recognized parameter for assessment of perfusion changes in peripheral tissues under different conditions. In outdoor breathing experiments with simulated avalanche snow, the subjects experience hypoxemia and hypercapnia due to significant rebreathing of the exhaled gas. In order to assess the behavior of the perfusion index during short-time hypoxemia and hypercapnia in these experiments, data from 13 healthy volunteers breathing into materials simulating avalanche snow were analyzed. The baseline perfusion index of the subjects at rest was 1.54+/-1.01. In the course of the experiment, despite the progressing hypoxemia and hypercapnia, there are no statistically significant changes in PI observed, followed by a rapid surge shortly after the subjects started to breathe ambient air and the hypercapnia prevailed over the vanishing hypoxemia. These results suggest that regardless of the hypoxemia and ambient environment, the perfusion of the peripheral tissues assessed by the pulse oximetry is sufficient during these experiments, presumably due to the vasodilatory effect of the hypercapnia.

articleTitle: Acrylic Self-curring Resin Biocompatibility - an in Vitro Study
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Current orthodontic practice employs the use of a wide variety of devices that have acrylic components. Due to its chemical composition, there has long been a concern about its biocompatibility in the oral environment. Through this study we aimed at determining the biocompatibility of the self-curing acrylate used in orthodontics. Our study was performed by analysing three study groups: the positive control group represented by copper amalgam fragments, the negative control group represented by human fibroblast cultures and the study group represented by self-curing acrylate fragments. The study groups were evaluated by means of microscopic analysis performed at three and six days with a Nikon Eclipse TE300 phase contrast microscope. Following the analysis at three days, a slight decrease in the concentration of fibroblasts around the material was noticed without revealing changes in shape. At six days an increase in cellular density similar to that of the control group was observed. Our study shows a good biocompatibility of in vitro self-polymerizing acrylate.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Apical Periodontitis using Running Maxima in Polar Coordinates
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: We introduce a novel method for the detection of apical periodontitis in radiography images, by combining image processing techniques, the partial transformation to polar coordinates and ideas from 1D signal processing, namely the running maximum. The algorithm has several adjustable parameters for adapting the method to various radiography resolutions and detail levels. Using a set of custom X-ray images where the affected region had been marked by a dentist, the approach is shown to have promising results, both in terms of overall evaluation and accuracy in identifying marked areas.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Manganese Retention in the Crustacean Tissue and its Implications for Chitin Product and Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: According to a principle of bio-economy, natural resources are the basis of numerous researches. Crustaceans are organisms with great biological diversity and importance in aquatic ecosystems, serving as bioindicators of the state of the environmental health. In addition to this, crustaceans represent a major source of obtaining chitin and chitosan. This study aims to evaluate the accumulation and storage of manganese ions, in four common species from the Romanian waters, Carcinus mediterraneus, Pachygrapsus marmoratus, Palaemon elegans, Euxinia maeotica. The purpose of the analysis is to obtain information upon the different accumulation of manganese, in soft structures or in exoskeleton, dependent of the biology of the species. This study also aims to understand the factors that ensure the efficiency of the extraction process of chitin from marine waste including different species of crustaceans. The obtained results highlighted that two species from sandy habitat (E. maeotica and C. mediterraneus) accumulate important amounts of manganese (80-100$\mu $g/g).

articleTitle: A Mobile App for ECG Monitoring Integrated in a Complex Home Care Platform
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The current paper describes a mobile app for recording ECG signals and for synchronizing health data with a complex home care platform for remote monitoring. The complex home care platform offers a multitude of features to home care providers and their clients. It contains a remote monitoring module that allows health data integration from multiple sources, including 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> party devices, using a public API. The proposed mobile app uses a device readily available on the market, Mintti HeartBook, to acquire and process the ECG signal and the before mentioned API to synchronize data with the platform. The platform offers web interfaces for data monitoring, alarm triggering functionalities and text/ video communications between medical personnel and patients.

articleTitle: Mathematical Models Regarding the Influence of Anterior Cranial Base Measurements over the Teeth and the Occlusal Plan
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Cephalometric analyses are decisive factors in the diagnosis and planning of orthodontic treatment. The anterior cranial base is a reference plan among them, because its growth influences the maxillofacial growth, and its modification affects the jaws position and the relationship between them, modifying the skeletal pattern and producing certain types of malocclusion. Our study aims to evaluate the influence of cephalometric measurements of the anterior cranial base on the cephalometric parameters concerning the teeth and the occlusal plane, through a mathematical model of multiple linear regression. We found that, regarding the teeth, the measurements with the biggest influence are NSGn (angle of Nasion-Sella-Gnathion) and SNA (angle of Sella-Nasion-A Point), and regarding the occlusal plan, the POr-OcP (angle of Frankfort line to occlusal plane) is mainly influenced by SN-OcP (angle of Sella-Nasion to occlusal plane), and the MeGoOcP (angle of Menton-Gonion to Occlusal plane) is mainly influenced also by NSGn (angle of Nasion-Sella-Gnathion).

articleTitle: Measurement of Tissue Heat Load Around a Transcutaneous Sensor Using a Thermal Imaging Camera - A Pilot Study
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The current trend in modern medicine is to use as many non-invasive techniques as possible, especially in the diagnostic process. Transcutaneous techniques, called tcp, are used to continuously monitor the evolution of partial blood pressures of O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, reducing the need for blood draws. The measuring element must induce a local hyperthermic effect; therefore, temperatures in the range of 38 to 44 °C are set. As the temperature increases, the accuracy of the measurement increases, but there is thermal stress on the tissue. This paper investigates the heat distribution around the tcp sensor using an infrared thermal imager.

articleTitle: Mobile Application to Improve the Therapy Process in Children with Delayed Speech Onset
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Currently, a considerable number of children suffer from late onset of speech, which occurs in infants from an early age having little interaction which develops a lack of communication between their surroundings. In this project we will focus on the late onset of speech and how to deal with it through the use of an application that manages to complement the sessions that are conducted with the specialist as well as reduce the time of these, generating economic savings and improvement for children. The research was of a technological applied type with an explanatory experimental design. The results were promising and indicate a great progress in the improvement of the children’s speech, it was identified that there was a reduction of 27.73% on the vocabulary learning time, the number of words learned increased by 123.67% and finally a reduction of 17.33% in the number of therapy sessions performed by each child was identified.

articleTitle: Printing of Dental Works from Cobalt-Chrome Metal Powder and Composite Material
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: Dental work can be made of a variety of materials, but this article shows how this type of work can be made of cobalt-chromium metal powders, respectively composite material; the processes to which these works are subjected are 3D modeling with the help of CAD software, respectively, the realization of the project in CAM software, to then be given to the 3D realization, so from virtual to physical. Everything is possible with the help of 3D prints on metal, MySint100 and composite material, Bego Varseo S.

articleTitle: Open Source Affordable Balance Testing based on a Nintendo Wii Balance Board
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: This paper presents an affordable balance testing board based on an algorithm called “the turning point for maintaining balance” for a desktop application that uses a Nintendo Wii balance board to gather accurate measures for further calculations. Two experts tested the accuracy of the application comparatively with a validated and expensive balance testing instrument. Accordingly, the solution gives precise measurements on a person’s balance in the form of curve length, area, Center of Pressure (COP), and turning point (TP). This paper shows the development of an open-source application and the corresponding research motivating affordable, functional screening possibilities.

articleTitle: Can Association Rules be Used to Improve Additive Bayesian Network Models?
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on e-Health and Bioengineering (EHB)
abstract: The study of antimicrobial resistance patterns is a challenging task due to the complexity of the mechanisms involved and the potentially large number of relations that must be inferred. Additive Bayesian networks have proved to be a useful tool in this respect, but when data is scarce, modeling results can be improved by integrating complementary information in the learning process. We propose an experimental study to investigate the benefits of including information extracted by association rule mining as prior knowledge into the inference of additive Bayesian networks.
